subject: ARLO SEO — Quarterly Review — Q3 2026
html:
ARLO SEO — Quarterly Review (Q3 2026)

Covering 2026-07-01 through 2026-09-30 (askarlo.app's first full quarter since the 2026-07-04 audit kickoff), reported 2026-10-01.

ROI bottom line

$0 attributable revenue or leads this quarter, and that's the expected number, not a miss: 12-week-strategy.md's own honest frame called this a 6–12 month organic ramp on a brand-new (DA 0) domain, with Month 1–3 KPIs defined as leading indicators — indexation, first tracked rankings, content/technical foundation — not leads. Measured against that bar, the quarter's real return is a fully-built foundation (every P0/P1 technical and structured-data defect from the original audit closed, both content engines — connector matrix and comparison hub — built out to exhaustion against the current product catalog, 43/43 shipped sessions with zero regressions) at the cost of engineering/content time only: no ad spend, no new paid tooling. The honest caveat: that foundation can't convert into rank or leads on its own. The three levers that actually move organic traffic — GSC submission, off-page link building (0 of 6 Phase 1 listings), and the 8 product connectors stuck in coming_soon (all 8 ETAs, May–August 2026, are now past due) — are all human-gated and all still untouched 3 months in. Until one of those moves, next quarter's ROI will look the same as this one's, regardless of how much more on-page work ships.

The quarter in 3 points

  1. Technical foundation is fully closed out. Every P0 critical from the 2026-07-04 audit (canonical bug, fabricated testimonials, broken structured data, dangling @id references, llms.txt errors) and every P1 quick win (FAQPage schema, per-page canonicals, noindex on app/auth routes, site-wide security headers, sitemap lastModified accuracy, the /privacy//terms sitemap gap) is shipped and verified. CI held 43/43 green all quarter across every push, with a build-gate (npm run build) on every session and zero shipped regressions.
  2. Both content engines are built out to exhaustion against the live product. The connector matrix (7/7 live data sources with dedicated /connect/[slug] pages), the comparison hub (5/5 named competitors — Supermetrics, AgencyAnalytics, Whatagraph, Funnel, Windsor), 5 /destinations/[slug] comparison sections (Looker Studio, Power BI, BigQuery, Tableau, Google Sheets), and 10 blog posts all shipped this quarter. Repeated fresh SE Ranking pulls (9+ consecutive sessions) confirm every remaining keyword with real demand (meta ads mcp, hubspot mcp, excel alternative, etc.) is gated on a catalog.ts connector or destination that doesn't exist yet — this routine has stopped shipping speculative pages rather than overclaim a feature that isn't live.
  3. Rank, backlinks, and AI visibility are flat for the entire quarter — and the cause is the untouched human-gated work, not a lack of content. All 22 tracked keywords sat at position 100 (not-ranked floor) every single day from kickoff through 2026-09-30; backlinks moved only incidentally, from 2/1 to 3/2 referring domains (Domain Trust 4→6); the AI Result Tracker still has zero LLM engines configured, so there's no AI-citation baseline at all. GSC submission (planned for Week 1) and off-page Phase 1 (planned for Week 4, 0 of 6 registries listed) are both still open 3 months after kickoff, and all 8 gated product connectors are now past their own ETAs.

Lead forecast vs. actual

MetricMonth-3 forecast (12-week-strategy.md)Actual (Q3 2026)
Keyword rankingsTop-20 for several low-KD connector/comparison terms0 of 22 tracked keywords ranked at all (position 100 every day)
Organic sessionsMeasurable organic sessions0 — SE Ranking's domain overview shows no ranking keywords in the US index
Leads / signups (GA4 conversions)Begin attributing signups/leadsPending — GA4 (G-CP22NBPLFP) has fired since kickoff, but this sandbox has no outbound GA4 Reporting API access; a human checking the GA4 console directly would close this out in minutes
Referring domains (off-page Phase 1)~6 from registries/Product Hunt by Week 40 of 6 — Phase 1 listings (Smithery, Glama, mcp.so, awesome-mcp-servers, AlternativeTo, SaaSHub) never started; the 3→2 backlink bump was incidental, not a shipped listing

Net: the quarter is behind its own Month-3 KPI ladder, but not because the on-page/technical work stalled — it's because the three off-site levers the ladder depended on (GSC submission, off-page outreach, timely connector launches) never moved. That's the single clearest thing a human can unblock before the next review.

Set up for Q4

  • Top priority, human-only: submit the sitemap in GSC and request indexing (open since Week 1, zero cost, likely the single highest-leverage action available) and configure at least one engine in SE Ranking's AI Result Tracker so AI-citation tracking has a baseline before Q4 closes.
  • Off-page Phase 1 (0 of 6) — Smithery.ai, Glama.ai, mcp.so, awesome-mcp-servers, AlternativeTo, SaaSHub — all free listings, all still unstarted after a full quarter.
  • Catalog connectors — all 8 gated integrations (meta_ads/linkedin_ads/meta_pages, tiktok_ads/stripe, hubspot/mailerlite, mailchimp) are now past their own ETAs; shipping any one of them unlocks the next connector-matrix page this routine has been ready to write for months.
  • Routine's own queue: re-read sxo.md end-to-end against current code (not yet re-checked this cycle, per the 2026-09-28 session's own note) for any remaining on-page gap, and keep re-pulling SE Ranking fresh each session — the Google Sheets and sitemap-legal-pages finds this quarter both came from treating "exhausted" as provisional, not permanent.
  • Still open, unchanged: a real Content-Security-Policy (needs live third-party-script testing this sandbox can't do), the www redirect mode (307→301/308, Vercel domain-config layer), IndexNow, and sxo.md #7 (a second case study/testimonial needs a real client quote, not something to invent).

Full session-by-session detail in docs/seo-strategy/worklog.txt.
